2/18.05.2023 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant and learned APP appearing on behalf of the State, assisted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2.
2.

This criminal appeal is directed against the order dated 12.04.2023, passed by the learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Dhanbad in connection with S.C./S.T. Case No. 21 of 2023 arising out of Rajganj P.S. Case No. 07 of 2023, registered under Sections 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 3(r), 3(s)
3(w)(ii) of the Scheduled Caste and the Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Atrocities) Act, but cognizance of the offence taken u/s 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 3(1) (r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(v)
of S.C./S.T. Act vide order dated 10.04.2023, whereby and whereunder the learned court dismissed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
3.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted on behalf of the appellant that the gist of allegations as presented in the FIR is that this appellant was establishing physical relationship with the victim since last three years under the promise of marriage and when the appellant denied to marry the informant, the case was instituted by the informant for the offence, inter alia, under section 376 of the IPC.
4. It has been submitted that the victim is aged about 28 years at the time of occurrence as evident from the FIR itself.

Further it has also been pointed out that both the parties including this appellant and the informant being the major have been establishing the physical relationship willingly and voluntarily since last three years, although the 2 Cr. 1 incident of physical relationship has been alleged to be forceful sexual assault of rape by the appellant and when the appellant after three years refused to marry and then this case was instituted.
5.

sentences.text:
It has further been pointed out that the charge-sheet in this case has been submitted, the appellant is in jail since 15/2/2023 and the possibility of tampering with the evidence is very remote.
6.

On the other hand, learned APP assisted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant vehemently opposed the contentions raised on behalf of the appellant and submitted that at first the appellant has committed rape with her and thereafter the promise of marriage was extended, but when he did not marry the informant and then the case was instituted.

It is also alleged that the appellant refused to marry with her by hurling abusive language by taking the name of the caste of the informant and therefore, he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
7.
Having heard the parties, perused the record of this case.

8. In the light of the aforesaid submission, the appellant is directed to be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court of learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Dhanbad, in Connection with S.C./S.T. Case No. 21 of 2023 arising out of Rajganj P.S. Case No. 07 of 2023,
subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., subject to the condition that he will cooperate in the case pending in the Court below and will appear on each and every date as and when required by the learned court below and the I.O., failing which the learned court below shall take appropriate steps for cancellation of the bail of the appellant.
9.

Accordingly, this appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 12.04.2023, passed by the learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Dhanbad, in connection with S.C./S.T. Case No. 21 of 2023,
arising out of Rajganj P.S. Case No. 07 of 2023 is set aside.
